prompt:
STYLE LOCK — Crystal Quest Painterly World Map.
Use the attached chapter-1-library-map.webp as the authoritative STYLE reference. Match its rendering, color relationships, material treatment, detail density and atmospheric depth, not its specific library building or geography.
Create a finely hand-painted premium fantasy mobile RPG world map. Use soft controlled painterly brush texture, delicate colored edges without black outlines, dimensional cream stone, naturally layered cliffs, nuanced lush foliage, tiny flowers and climbing ivy. Use warm sunlight, cool teal-violet shadows, golden paths, turquoise water where appropriate, blue atmospheric distance and softly billowing white clouds. Violet-blue crystals have translucent faceted surfaces, white highlights and restrained magical glow; gold is a restrained waypoint accent.
Use an elevated three-quarter map view, clear destination architecture, readable winding routes, crisp nearby terrain and softer lower-contrast distant scenery. Keep navigation landmarks distinct at portrait mobile size. The image must look like another region painted by the same artist as the style reference. Preserve the region's own subject and geography rather than copying the reference's buildings.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Wordoria Crystal Quest World 6B scrollable story world map, corrected 20-stage version.
Primary request: World 6B Road to the Royal Capital. Exactly TWENTY stages, progressing TOP TO BOTTOM, never bottom to top. User correction overrides the incomplete runtime.
Reference roles: Image 1 = chapter-1-library-map.webp, authoritative painterly STYLE. Image 2 = obsolete World 6B one-stage proposal, subject/material reference only; its layout is explicitly superseded. Completely replace its route direction, city location and waypoint count. Do NOT put the capital at the top. Do NOT reuse its single waypoint layout.
Composition: very tall portrait approximately 1:3, target 1024 x 3072. Elevated three-quarter view, a long continuous gently serpentine golden road progressing DOWN the image. The TOP is the START: a small empty campsite beside a cave exit in green forest foothills. The MIDDLE is the JOURNEY: lush hills, flower-lined forest roads, a bandit roadblock clearing at stage 10 (a parked wagon, crates and displaced timber barricades, no people), a turquoise stream and one cream-stone bridge. The BOTTOM is the DESTINATION: the royal capital in the lowest quarter of the image, open city gates, cream-stone walls, blue-violet roofs, townhouses, castle and knight commander's manor arranged beside and behind the final road section. Show all important architecture inside the canvas. Place the final stage in the capital's welcoming paved plaza near the bottom. No castle or city skyline at the top. No horizon or scenic filler that displaces the topmost stages. Top and bottom progress refer to 2D screen coordinates; all buildings remain upright, do not rotate the art.
Gameplay contract: exactly 20 separate violet-blue crystal waypoints on exactly 20 gold-rimmed circular pedestals, along ONE connected road in numbered sequence without drawing any numbers. Every successive pedestal is strictly lower in screen y than the previous one. Slight lateral winding is allowed, but no upward retracing, disconnected islands, branching paths, extra pedestals, hidden markers or missing crystals. Crystals should be large enough to count individually on mobile. Calm open landing around each pedestal. Avoid decorative violet crystals elsewhere; any incidental cyan minerals must have no pedestal.

Maintain warm upper-left daylight, soft painterly foliage, layered cream cliffs, atmospheric clouds around land edges, restrained turquoise water and violet crystal accents. No library, no unrelated temple, no signs or text.

Avoid coarse low-poly geometry, chunky toy-like 3D rendering, plastic surfaces, flat oversaturated green terrain, black cartoon outlines, pixel art, gritty photorealism, muddy dark palettes, excessive bloom and repetitive noisy detail. No characters, monsters, text, letters, numbers, UI, labels, logos, watermark, frames or black side borders. Do not obscure the route or waypoint crystals with foliage, clouds or effects. Do not introduce buildings or narrative elements unrelated to the requested world.


TARGETED EDIT OF IMAGE 2, KEEP THE REST OF THE MAP UNCHANGED: Image 2 mistakenly has TWENTY-FIVE crystal pedestals. Remove exactly FIVE existing crystal-and-gold-pedestal assemblies completely and paint ordinary golden path in their place, retaining road continuity. Read normalized coordinates from upper-left.
